answer: Each seat owns one lot of timber in a bonded yard, tagged with a lot number logged by a licensed scaler at arrival. Each epoch the seed names a lot; within a day the scaler re-measures that stack, notes board feet, moisture and the stamp, then signs. Lots sharing one yard licence, or one arrival date and hauler, fold into a single vote and forfeit 90,000 POA each. Space and insurance run $46 per tonne-month, so a thousand seats means two thousand tonnes held, some $92,000 monthly. A relic of the trade, the stamp holds because wet timber keeps a mark no clerk fakes from across the horizon.
